chapter: Silver Leaf and the Tuxedo Band
title: Silver Leaf, meeting Celestin and founding the Tuxedo Band
summary: Around 1910-11 he moves to New Orleans, meets Celestin through Welch, and the two organize the Tuxedo Band after the old district closes.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Do you remember about, excuse me, what year that was about? Was that...

That could have been about 1910. 1910, when you joined the Silver Leaf. Silver Leaf Band. I was still living in Jefferson Paris. And then I moved to New Orleans in 1911. And I was still with Silver Leaf Band. And Mr. Welch, he was a sickly man and he gave up the coinette playing. And we got over to the fellow by the name of Hippolyte Charles. He played coinette for us a while. And then he gave up the coinette playing and old man Welch came back again. And old man Welch made me to know Celestine. He said he was a very fine fellow and he think would make a good coinette player. And that we would try to use him. So we got acquainted with Celestine and he got us with us. And he played along in Silver Leaf Band with me. And then later he got a job playing in the old district at the 101 Ranch. And him and I went in the district to play together. And we joined in with another bunch of fellows. And when the old district closed, then him and I organized the Tuxedo Band. He was playing there but I never did. And we joined the Tuxedo Band and we got another bunch of fellows. Around 1914 we were still in the old district. And I think then it came to close again. And we got our band out in the field. We call it the Tuxedo Jazz Band. Celestine, myself, Johnny Lindsay, Ernest Trapani, Lorenzo Teo, Peter... Who was the river? Peter Bocard. Peter Bocard. And that was our boy stand. And from that we went on and doing pretty good. And something happened that some of those men left. But Celestine and I still was together. And then I got me a band headquarters on Howard Avenue between Drys and Barone. And run the Preston Shop and the Shoe Black stand. And that was our headquarters. And from that on we began to grow faster. And getting in much work, I got to know a white gentleman by the name of Sim Black. He was scoutmaster of Boy Scout Troop Thirteen. And he used to visit our band quarters pretty regularly. So one day he came in and he said originally, he said, I have a suggestion for you. He said, something I think will improve the band. And he said, I was thinking that if you all would get black tuxedo suit, derby hat, white shirts, said, and I think it would help the band a great deal. And that was just about the time for the deputy season to open. And that time, the late Henry Zeno was playing drums for me. And he taken up on him to go out to find a tuxedo suit. We find him at the mass, that ain't right. Is there a tailor shop you found them? Yes, tailor shop. And it cost us $15 a piece. And from then on, our band just went on like a blaze of fire. And we used to play during the wartime. Played at Heinemann Park every Sunday for the baseball season. We played every year on the 6th of January for the 12th Night Revlon at the Arthenaire. We played all of the great ball, mostly for all of the carnival clubs. And we were well thought of by the people. And in 1923, we went to Fort Worth with the Pelicans on the southern season with the police band of New Orleans. And some ladies from Texas know that our band were coming and asked us what would we charge them to play a half an hour. They were raising a $25,000 milk fund. And we agreed to play for them for nothing. They treated us good, taking us all over Fort Worth. And police band was very nice to us. And on our way back in New Orleans, then we played in the largest chair in the world that had been all around the world. Taking the bass, violin, drums, and the whole band put it up on a truck. Now the tuxedo band, we called it the Tuxedo Jazz Band. But Mr. Sim Black suggested that we would call the band the original Tuxedo Band. And that's who named the band at that time.
